plan_a_advantages: It prioritizes recovery through frequent easy runs.
The shorter, more frequent runs might be suitable for someone very new to trail running or recovering from an injury.
plan_b_advantages: Includes a dedicated aerobic session for building a base.
Gradually increases run duration, promoting adaptation and improved endurance.
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. While Plan A focuses almost entirely on very easy runs, which can be beneficial for recovery, it lacks any structured stimulus for improving speed or endurance. Plan B incorporates a dedicated aerobic session and gradually increases the duration of easy runs, providing a more progressive approach to building a solid aerobic base – a crucial component for trail running speed. The longer, consistent easy runs in Plan B will contribute more to overall fitness and stamina than the repetitive short easy runs in Plan A.
